title: Early release of convicted rapist Max Factor heir Andrew Luster sparks outrage in Glendora
text:
Early release of convicted rapist Max Factor heir Andrew Luster sparks outrage in Glendora - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Early release of convicted rapist Max Factor heir Andrew Luster sparks outrage in Glendora 
 People in the city of Glendora are furious about the early release of convicted rapist and Andrew Luster, the heir to the Max Factor cosmetics fortune. Tuesday, October 20, 2026 11:51PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google GLENDORA, Calif. (CNS) -- A Glendora-area state assemblywoman is pledging to push for stronger safeguards for communities after word that Max Factor cosmetics heir and convicted serial rapist Andrew Luster was released from state prison this month and was residing there.
 California's Megan's Law website confirmed the 62-year-old Luster was living in Glendora.
 Assemblywoman Blanca E. Rubio said Luster's release "is disgusting and unacceptable. I am working closely with local officials and law enforcement to stay informed about the circumstances of Luster's release, the conditions of his parole and the measures being taken to protect the residents of Glendora and surrounding communities."
 Luster was originally sentenced to 124 years in prison after he was convicted in 2003 of 86 felony counts related to rendering women unconscious with the date rape drug GHB and committing rape, sodomy and oral copulation on them while they were unconscious. Evidence included video he made of himself in those acts.
 He was released after serving about 20 years, Rubio said.
 Glendora Mayor David Fredendall said Luster's release was expedited by Proposition 57, which voters approved in 2016, when then-Gov. Jerry Brown made assurances that sex offenders would not be eligible for parole.
 "Our Police Department will work with State parole authorities to ensure every applicable law and condition of supervision is followed," Fredendall said in a statement. "We will do everything within our lawful authority to protect our residents."
 Rubio said she was a co-author of Senate Bill 268 in 2024 which closed a loophole that classified rapes of unconscious or drugged victims as non-violent offenses, changing it to a violent felony.
 She promised to work with local officials, law enforcement and legislative colleagues to make sure "Justice must not end with a conviction. It must also mean accountability, protection for victims and confidence our justice system puts public safety first."
